pilot: T1,T3,T7 x 2 trials x {A,B_default} = 12 scored trials
headline_finding: 0 of 12 scored trials reached task_success=True in EITHER arm. The frozen protocol's max_steps=8 budget was insufficient for any of T1/T3/T7 to reach a written, graded answer -- every non-crashed trial exhausted its 8 tool calls in exploration (stop_reason=step_budget, files_touched=[]) before ever writing answer.md. This is a real, honest pilot result: it validates the mechanism runs end-to-end for real money on real infrastructure, but the chosen budget cannot be evaluated for success-rate or success-normalized-efficiency from this data -- both arms are tied at 0%, which is not evidence of parity, it is an unmeasured comparison due to an underpowered budget.

pre_fix_environmental_failures.reason: run_pilot.py's first invocation loaded .env only into the MCP-server subprocess, not this orchestrator process's own os.environ; GENERAL_COMPUTE_API_KEY was missing for in-process calls (arm A always, arm B's in-process retrieval). Zero tokens spent on any of the 5. Fixed before any scored trial ran (see trials.jsonl's environmental_failure=true rows and orchestrator run_pilot.py's own bugfix comment).

B_default.error_type: ExceptionGroup: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (2 sub-exceptions), identical both trials
B_default.note: both B_default trials crashed with no usage/retrieval data captured -- see reliability_finding below

success_normalized_efficiency.reason: Per the frozen protocol's own dominance rule (success before efficiency), success-normalized comparison requires at least one successful trial per cell to normalize against. 0 of 12 scored trials succeeded in either arm on any task. Reporting a raw-token or raw-latency 'winner' here would violate the protocol's explicit instruction that a lower-token run which is incorrect is NOT a win -- so none is reported.

reliability_finding.description: T7 (the composition task) is the only cell showing an asymmetry between arms: arm A completed both trials to a graceful step-budget exhaustion (no crash, real token usage captured, real partial exploration happened) both times; arm B_default hard-crashed with an identical ExceptionGroup both times, before any usage or Stealth-decision data could even be captured. This pattern is 100% reproducible across both trials of that one cell (n=2) and does not appear in any of the other 8 non-crashed trials (T1 and T3's B_default trials both ran to completion without error).
reliability_finding.root_cause: DIAGNOSED (found in experiments/swebench_pro/'s own auto-generated failed-request dumps, relocated to raw/provider_400_errors/ -- 6 files, all a real BadRequestError('Provider request failed with status 400') from GENERAL_COMPUTE, occurring at various steps (3, 3, 3, 4, 7, 7) across MULTIPLE trials during this run, not only the two that crashed. This is a real, intermittent GENERAL_COMPUTE provider reliability issue. In most trials it appears to have been absorbed/retried internally (those trials still completed with real token usage); the working hypothesis is that T7 (the largest-scope task) makes more than one such call inside the same asyncio TaskGroup, and when 2 of them 400 close together, both surface as sub-exceptions in one unhandled ExceptionGroup instead of being individually retried.
reliability_finding.classification: REAL, DIAGNOSED FINDING (upgraded from insufficient_evidence after inspecting the auto-generated request dumps): a genuine GENERAL_COMPUTE provider-reliability issue that the current execution path does not defend against when multiple failures land inside one TaskGroup. This is arguably a genuine product/harness robustness gap (no per-call retry/backoff around transient 400s in this execution path) rather than a Stealth-specific defect, but it disproportionately affects the Stealth-enabled arm on the largest task because that arm appears to issue more concurrent calls.
reliability_finding.evidence_files: raw/provider_400_errors/failed_request_local_agent_*.json (6 files, secrets-scanned clean, real system prompts + real error bodies)

stealth_retrieval_quality_finding.description: In the 4 B_default trials that ran to completion (T1 x2, T3 x2), Stealth's real retrieval matched a procedure in all 4 -- but independently queried against the live DB, both matched procedures turn out to be synthetic e2e-test fixtures ('proc-test-planonly-root-*', whose name AND goal fields are literally the same auto-generated fixture string), not real, task-relevant knowledge. T1's match is identical to the one this session's earlier smoke test also matched, for a completely unrelated trivial task -- suggesting this fixture may be an easy/generic lexical match that surfaces regardless of real task content.
stealth_retrieval_quality_finding.implication: This is a corpus-contamination finding, not a retrieval-mechanism bug: the mechanism correctly executed a real search and returned a real top hit, but the CORPUS it searched is ~99% engineering-fixture noise (confirmed by this session's own earlier Finding D characterization), so for a genuinely novel task with no real matching knowledge yet admitted, retrieval surfaces irrelevant noise rather than correctly returning 'no match'. Whether the agent actually acted on this irrelevant match (wasted a step investigating it) vs. ignored it could not be determined from the captured node_notes this pass -- worth a closer look before the full matrix.

budget_finding.description: In every non-crashed trial across all 3 tasks and both arms, model_calls landed at exactly 5-8 and tool_calls at exactly 8 (the hard max_steps ceiling) with stop_reason=step_budget and files_touched=[] -- the agent was still exploring, never reached the point of writing an answer file, in 10 of 10 non-crashed trials.
budget_finding.implication: max_steps=8 is very likely too tight for T1/T3/T7 as designed, independent of Stealth. This is a task/budget calibration finding, not a Stealth finding -- both arms hit it equally. Per the frozen protocol's own 'no mid-experiment changes' rule, this was NOT adjusted mid-pilot; it is reported as the top recommendation for revising the protocol before a full-matrix run.
